title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap, Pricing & Q4 2028 Release Notes
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This document consolidates the product overview, PRD-level requirements, high-level design notes, roadmap themes, pricing and packaging decisions, and release notes for the Unified Inference product family (v28) as delivered in Q4 2028. It is intended for product managers, engineering leads, solutions engineering, and GTM. The document summarizes what shipped in the Q4 release, why the work was prioritized, and the rollout and monitoring plans.

Goals

- Deliver a single, consistent inference experience across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Reduce per-token cost by 18-25% on common text generation workloads via runtime improvements, smarter routing, and new quantization profiles.
- Provide a clearer pricing/packaging surface that aligns to developer and enterprise buying motions.
- Improve reliability of long-chat workloads (>=8k context) with KV-cache persistence and progressive fallback.

Key Features Shipped (v28, Q4 2028)

- Multi-tier routing policies: latency-first, cost-first, and compliance-first.
- Persistent KV-cache for session affinity and long-context workloads (opt-in).
- On-the-fly quantization profile selection based on model and request distribution.
- New pricing tiers and per-route cost controls in Redwood Console.
- API: batch streaming endpoint and improved function/tool calling fidelity for structured outputs.

Product Requirements (PRD summary)

Primary personas:
1. ML Engineer (serving-focused): needs predictable throughput and cost controls.
2. Product developer (PLG): needs simple API, free-tier to trial, and predictable billing.
3. Platform/Infra (enterprise): needs VPC/private deployment, KMS integration, and audit logs.

Top-level success metrics:
- Reduce mean per-token cost (production workload) by >=18% for targeted workloads.
- 99.9% availability for hosted low-latency tier across primary regions.
- Increase PLG-to-Dedicated conversion rate by 12% in target accounts within 90 days.
- Latency SLO: p95 generation latency <= 250ms for <512 token requests on low-latency tier.

Requirements table (summary):

| Requirement ID | Description | Priority | Owner | Acceptance criteria |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| PRD-UI-001 | Per-route cost controls in Console | M | product/console | UI exposes overrides, backend enforces limits, e2e test coverage |
| PRD-RTE-010 | KV-cache persistence with TTL and invalidation API | H | eng-serving-runtime | Cache hit >= 30% on target workloads, API to purge/session invalidate |
| PRD-RTG-005 | Multi-tier routing policies | H | eng-platform | Routing rules evaluate latency/cost/region and fall back to compatible model variants |
| PRD-SH-020 | New pricing tiers and free credits for PLG | H | finance/product | Billing changes test, migrations plan, pricing docs updated |

Design summary (high level)

- Runtime changes: introduce a persistent KV-cache layer that sits between request router and the serving runtime. Cache entries are indexed by model-id + session-id + prefix-hash. The cache supports TTL, explicit invalidation, and a resident memory budget per customer.

- Routing: policy engine evaluates per-request signals (latency SLA, region, customer tier, cost budget) and selects a target model variant and serving pool. Policies are declarative JSON stored in the control plane and can be updated via API.

- Quantization profiles: compile-time kernel selection augmented with a light-weight runtime estimator that picks between int8/4/quant-fp strategies based on sequence length and model topology.

- Console changes: new per-route cost and latency dashboard, rollout controls (canary/A/B), and pricing tier selector.

APIs and examples

1) Example: enable persistent KV-cache for a session (CLI):

redwood-cli sessions enable-cache --session-id sess-1234 --model redwood-v7 --ttl 72h

2) Example: routing policy snippet (declarative):

{
  "policy_name": "latency-first-eu",
  "priority": ["latency", "region", "cost"],
  "rules": [
    {"if": "region == 'eu' && latency_sla <= 200", "target": "low-latency-pool"},
    {"else": "fallback-compatible-quantized"}
  ]
}

Note: above is illustrative; exact JSON schema is in eng-platform/policies repo.

Roadmap & Themes (next 6 quarters)

Q1 2029: Expand persistent KV-cache to Dedicated/offline on-prem packages; SLA hardening and cross-region replication.
Q2 2029: Model-level evaluation hooks in the Console with A/B quality monitoring and automated rollback.
Q3 2029: Latency-aware autoscaling (predictive) and improved kernel packing for very long sequences.
Q4 2029: Pricing experimentation and marketplace integrations for channel partners.

Cross-cutting themes:
- Developer-first observability: better per-token attribution, prompt-set linked regressions.
- Cost-awareness: actionable suggestions, automatic batch sizing hints.
- Enterprise readiness: enhanced audit trails, KMS/HSM rotation policies.

Pricing & Packaging Notes

New 2028 pricing tiers (announced in this release):
- Developer (free tier): 1M tokens/month free for 30 days + pay-as-you-go after credits.
- Growth: per-token priced with burst-capacity; includes Console per-route controls.
- Enterprise: committed reserved capacity (monthly minimum), dedicated pools, and priority routing.

Per-route billing examples:
- Typical chat session (1k tokens) on Growth: base rate $0.0009/token -> $0.90/session before discounts.
- With persistent KV-cache hit (30%): effective tokens billed 700 -> $0.63/session.

Migration and billing notes:
- Existing customers on v25/v26 tiers will be automatically migrated to comparable Growth/Enterprise tiers with pro-rated credits. Finance will run a migration script and email impacted customers 30 days prior.

Release Notes (v28, 2028-11-01)

Highlights:
- Persistent KV-cache (opt-in) with session TTL and admin purge API.
- Multi-tier routing with declarative policies and automatic fallback to quantized variants.
- Console: per-route cost controls, new pricing tier selector, and per-route dashboards.
- API: batch streaming endpoint (beta) and improved function calling fidelity.

Bug fixes and perf improvements:
- Reduced p95 token generation latency by 12% in low-latency pool across small-model workloads.
- Fixed session leak causing increased memory pressure in certain Dedicated configs.
- Quantization: corrected rounding error affecting logits for int4 on a subset of models.

Known issues:
- KV-cache invalidation under concurrent session-migration scenarios can temporarily return stale prefixes (edge case). A patch is scheduled for 2028-11-14. Workaround: explicit session purge via CLI/API.

Rollout & Deployment Plan

1) Canary (Week 0-1): 5% of traffic routed to v28 pools in us-west-2 and eu-central-1. Monitor p95 latency, error rate, and cache hit rate.
2) Gradual increase (Week 2-4): expand to 25% then 60% based on health gates.
3) Opt-in features (KV-cache): enabled by customer opt-in; default off for Hosted.
4) Enterprise migrations (Week 3-8): contact-managed with support and billing coordination.

Health gates (must-pass to progress):
- p95 latency regression < 3% relative to baseline.
- Error rate delta < 0.1% absolute.
- Cache hit rate >= expected threshold (20% for targeted workloads).

Monitoring and KPIs

Primary dashboards to monitor:
- Per-route cost (tokens, billed tokens, effective cost).
- Cache metrics: hit rate, eviction rate, memory usage per-customer.
- Routing decisions: percent by policy, fallbacks per-hour.
- Quality regressions: per-prompt-set BLEU/ROUGE/LLM-eval scores (linked tests).

2. Decide whether to enable persistent KV-cache.
3. Validate billing changes in a staging account.
4. Schedule migration window and support contact.
